Both also cover print by embedding the font in the PDF. B explains more clearly what readers see when the font fails to load (Segoe UI on library Windows PCs, Roboto on Android) and tells the user to test with a real print, a photocopy and an old Android phone. A never suggests testing on real devices. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend a sensible free, open-licensed sans for web and print and give self-hosted CSS with a generic fallback at the end. A ends with specific checks: a test print, a photocopy and the oldest Android phone available. B never mentions testing on real devices, though it has more layout tips and a simple system-font-only option.
